findings.location: Poem, stanza 4 (line: "The devil smiles as he tightens our collar.")
findings.source_quote: The devil smiles as he tightens our collar.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate collar idiomatically. Replace "aperta nosso colar" with "aperta nosso colarinho" or "aperta nosso pescoço" (depending on tone). A good fix: "O diabo sorri enquanto aperta nosso colarinho."
findings.translation_quote: O diabo sorri enquanto aperta nosso colar.

findings.location: Poem, stanza 7 (line: "But money will bind us until death we meet.")
findings.source_quote: But money will bind us until death we meet.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the straightforward sense: that money binds us until we die. Replace the current translation with an idiomatic equivalent that does not add or alter meaning. Suggested fix: "Mas o dinheiro nos prende até encontrarmos a morte." or better: "Mas o dinheiro nos prende até a morte."
findings.translation_quote: Mas o dinheiro nos prende até encontrarmos a morte ao morrer.

findings.location: Poem, stanza 8 (line: "The more we have, the more we need; / The love of money starts with a seed.")
findings.source_quote:
The more we have, the more we need;
The love of money starts with a seed.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not add actors or causation not in the original. Remove the added phrase "que semeamos." Use a faithful, natural rendering such as: "Quanto mais temos, mais precisamos; / O amor ao dinheiro começa com uma semente."
findings.translation_quote:
Quanto mais temos, mais precisamos;
O amor ao dinheiro começa com uma semente que semeamos.

findings.location: Poem, stanza 9 (final line: "'Freedom, or bondage?' is the question I bring.")
findings.source_quote: "Freedom, or bondage?" is the question I bring.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not introduce unrelated context ("à escola"). Translate the line simply and literally in Portuguese. Suggested fix: "'Liberdade, ou escravidão?' é a pergunta que trago."
findings.translation_quote: “Liberdade, ou escravidão?” é a pergunta que trago à escola.
